paragraphs.text: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an autosomal recessive disorder that appears within the first weeks of life. Affected infants cannot absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine. The resulting severe diarrhea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet (Turk et al., 1991). The disorder is caused by a defect in the Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1 of the intestinal brush border (Martín et al., 1996).

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, the resulting severe diarrhea and dehydration are usually fatal unless glucose and galactose are removed from the diet.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is caused by a defect in the Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1 of the intestinal brush border.

checks.explanation: The abstract says GGM is caused by a defect in SGLT1, the intestinal brush-border cotransporter.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) studied glucose transport by jejunal mucosa in vitro and by the kidney in vivo in a 3-year-old girl with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption, in her family, and in 16 normal volunteers. Biopsy specimens from 6 normal controls and from the proband's asymptomatic 5-year-old brother accumulated glucose to 16 times the concentration in the incubation medium. The proband's mucosa could not concentrate glucose at any point during a 60-minute incubation. All subjects accumulated fructose to a similar degree. Renal glucose titration showed a partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption in the proband, whereas her brother's titration curve was similar to those of 7 normal volunteers. The authors concluded that absent intestinal glucose transport is accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) found impaired jejunal glucose transport in both parents and a half sister of a patient with glucose-galactose malabsorption. Their values fell between those of normal controls and that of the proband. In these heterozygotes, glucose influx was impaired but glucose efflux was the same as in normal controls. Kinetic analysis showed a reduced capacity (Vmax) with normal affinity (Km) for glucose transport. The authors concluded that familial glucose-galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait and that heterozygotes can be detected.

paragraphs.text: Martín et al. (1996) noted that 2 proband sibs with GGM from a large consanguineous family had previously been shown to carry the D28N mutation in SGLT1, which accounts for their defect in sugar absorption. They screened 2 later pregnancies in this family for D28N by EcoRV restriction digestion of PCR-amplified exon 1. The proband's sib was heterozygous for the mutation, and a cousin was not a carrier. Both children were healthy at 2 years of age.

paragraphs.text: Xin and Wang (2011) studied 33 Old Order Amish patients with GGM from a large pedigree. Among the homozygous missense mutations they identified in the SLC5A1 gene was a c.152A-G transition, resulting in an asn51-to-ser (N51S) substitution. It was 1 of 4 homozygous missense mutations that cosegregated with the GGM phenotype in all affected individuals.
